We need maximize the volume of an ellipsoid inside the centrally symmetric polytope \(K\).

Let an ellipsoid centered at \(0\) be
\[
E=T B_4,\qquad M=TT^T\succeq 0.
\]
Since \(K=-K\), any ellipsoid \(c+TB_4\subset K\) gives, by reflection and convexity,
\[
TB_4=\frac12\bigl((c+TB_4)+(-c+TB_4)\bigr)\subset K,
\]
with the same volume. So it suffices to consider centered ellipsoids.

For a slab \(|a^Tx|\le 1\), the condition \(TB_4\subset\{|a^Tx|\le1\}\) is
\[
a^TMa\le1.
\]
Thus we maximize
\[
\det M=\left(\frac{\operatorname{vol}(E)}{\operatorname{vol}(B_4)}\right)^2
\]
subject to the six inequalities from
\[
e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4,\quad s=(1,1,1,1),\quad t=\left(\frac13,\frac13,\frac13,-1\right).
\]

The first three coordinates are symmetric, so averaging over their permutations preserves feasibility and does not decrease \(\det M\). Hence the optimizer has form
\[
M=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&b&b&c\\
b&a&b&c\\
b&b&a&c\\
c&c&c&d
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Set
\[
p=a-b,\qquad q=a+2b.
\]
Then
\[
\det M=p^2(qd-3c^2),
\]
and the constraints become
\[
a=\frac{q+2p}{3}\le1,\qquad d\le1,
\]
\[
3q+6c+d\le1,\qquad \frac q3-2c+d\le1.
\]
For fixed \(q\), the determinant is increasing in \(p\), so
\[
p=\frac{3-q}{2}.
\]
Now maximize
\[
qd-3c^2
\]
under
\[
d\le 1-3q-6c,\qquad d\le 1-\frac q3+2c.
\]
For fixed \(q\), the best \(d\) is the smaller of those two upper bounds. The first decreases in \(c\), the second increases in \(c\), so the maximum occurs where they meet:
\[
1-3q-6c=1-\frac q3+2c.
\]
Thus
\[
c=-\frac q3,\qquad d=1-q.
\]
Then
\[
qd-3c^2=q(1-q)-\frac{q^2}{3}=q-\frac43q^2.
\]
So
\[
\det M=\frac{(3-q)^2}{4}\left(q-\frac43q^2\right)
=\frac1{12}q(3-q)^2(3-4q),
\]
with \(0<q<\frac34\).

Differentiate:
\[
\frac{d}{dq}\log\bigl(q(3-q)^2(3-4q)\bigr)
=\frac1q-\frac2{3-q}-\frac4{3-4q}.
\]
Setting this to zero gives
\[
16q^2-33q+9=0.
\]
The admissible root is
\[
q=\frac{33-3\sqrt{57}}{32}.
\]
Substituting,
\[
\det M
=\frac1{12}q(3-q)^2(3-4q)
=\frac{81(133\sqrt{57}-471)}{131072}.
\]

Therefore,
\[
\boxed{\frac{81(133\sqrt{57}-471)}{131072}}.
\]
